question: Who among the following is considered the most powerful Chola ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajaraja I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajaraja I (राजराजा प्रथम) (reigned c. 985–1014 CE) is regarded as the greatest and most powerful ruler of the Chola dynasty.

• He expanded the Chola empire across South India, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, and built a powerful navy.

• He built the magnificent Rajarajeshwara (Brihadeeswarar) Temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• His son Rajendra I further extended Chola power up to the Ganga and Southeast Asia.

• The Cholas are famous for their local self-government and elaborate village administration (Uttaramerur inscriptions).

NOTE

• Dantidurga (Option 1): Founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the 8th century, not a Chola ruler.

• Harshvardhan (Option 2): 7th-century ruler of Kannauj (Pushyabhuti dynasty) in North India.

• Virarajendra Chola (Option 3): A later Chola ruler, far less powerful than Rajaraja I.

question: After the Tughlaqs, which two dynasties ruled Agra until 1526?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sayyids and Lodis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the Tughlaq dynasty, the Sayyid (सैय्यद) and Lodi (लोदी) dynasties ruled the Delhi Sultanate (including Agra) until 1526.

• The Sayyid dynasty (1414–1451) was founded by Khizr Khan.

• The Lodi dynasty (1451–1526) was founded by Bahlul Lodi; Sikandar Lodi shifted the capital to Agra in 1504.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Lodi rule ended with Ibrahim Lodi's defeat by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat (1526), establishing the Mughal Empire.

• The five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate: Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid and Lodi.

NOTE

• Sur and Khaljis (Option 1): The Sur dynasty (Sher Shah) ruled 1540–1555, after the Mughals began; Khaljis ruled before the Tughlaqs.

• Tughlaqs and Mughals (Option 2): Mughals came only after 1526; Tughlaqs preceded the Sayyids.

• Khiljis and Lodis (Option 3): The Khaljis ruled 1290–1320, well before the Tughlaqs.

question: Which of the following article of Indian Constitution ensures the protection of minority interests?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 29.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 29 (अनुच्छेद 29) protects the interests of minorities by allowing any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture to conserve it.

• It falls under the Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29–30) in the Fundamental Rights.

• It also prohibits denial of admission to state-aided educational institutions on grounds of religion, race, caste or language.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 30 gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

• Fundamental Rights are contained in Part III (Articles 12–35) of the Constitution.

NOTE

• Article 28 (Option 1): Freedom regarding attendance at religious instruction in certain educational institutions.

• Article 24 (Option 2): Prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories and hazardous work.

• Article 31 (Option 3): Right to property (repealed by the 44th Amendment, 1978).

question: The National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) completed its 5 years in _____ 2025.
solution_text:
The correct answer is July.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Education Policy 2020 (राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति 2020) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 July 2020, so it completed 5 years in July 2025.

• It replaced the earlier National Policy on Education of 1986.

• It was drafted by a committee headed by Dr. K. Kasturirangan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• NEP 2020 introduced the 5+3+3+4 curricular and pedagogical structure replacing the 10+2 system.

• It aims for a Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) of 50% in higher education by 2035 and 6% of GDP spending on education.

NOTE

• January (Option 1): Not the month of NEP 2020's approval.

• March (Option 2): Not associated with NEP 2020's adoption.

• April (Option 4): Marked wrong in the response sheet; NEP was approved in July, not April.

question: How many female cadets passed out in the first-ever batch at National Defence Academy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first-ever batch of female cadets — 17 women (17 महिला कैडेट) — passed out from the National Defence Academy (NDA), Khadakwasla, Pune in 2025.

• They were part of the 148th course, the first to admit women following a 2021 Supreme Court ruling.

• The NDA is a tri-services (Army, Navy, Air Force) training academy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Women were inducted into the NDA for the first time in 2022 after a landmark Supreme Court judgment.

• The NDA was established in 1954 and is located at Khadakwasla near Pune, Maharashtra.

NOTE

• 11 (Option 1): Not the number of female cadets in the first passing-out batch.

• 19 (Option 3): Incorrect figure for the first women's batch.

• 21 (Option 4): Incorrect figure for the first women's batch.

question: In July 2025, Indian government launched "SOAR" initiative. This initiative targets_____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is AI-skilling grades 6–12 school students.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The SOAR (Skilling for AI Readiness) initiative targets AI-skilling of school students in grades 6–12 (कक्षा 6–12 के छात्रों का एआई-कौशल).

• It was launched to prepare young students for an AI-driven future through age-appropriate AI education.

• The programme integrates AI awareness and skills into the school ecosystem.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The initiative aligns with the vision of NEP 2020 to promote future-ready skills and digital literacy.

• AI-based learning modules and teacher orientation form key components of the programme.

NOTE

• Training women entrepreneurs in e-commerce (Option 1): Not the focus of the SOAR initiative.

• Upskilling artisans under PM Vishwakarma (Option 3): PM Vishwakarma is a separate scheme for traditional artisans and craftspeople.

• Vocational training for gig workers (Option 4): Not the objective of SOAR.

question: With a view to boost technical textiles sector in the country, National Technical Textiles Mission (NTTM) was launched for a period from _____ with an outlay of Rs.1,480 crores.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020-21 to 2025-26.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Technical Textiles Mission (राष्ट्रीय तकनीकी वस्त्र मिशन) was launched for the period 2020-21 to 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs. 1,480 crore.

• It aims to make India a global leader in technical textiles and boost domestic production.

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Mission has four components: research & innovation, promotion & market development, export promotion, and education/skilling.

• Technical textiles include applications in agriculture, defence, healthcare (Meditech), infrastructure and geotextiles.

NOTE

• 2022-23 to 2026-27 (Option 1): Incorrect period for NTTM.

• 2021-22 to 2024-25 (Option 2): Incorrect period for NTTM.

• 2022-23 to 2025-26 (Option 4): Incorrect period for NTTM.

question: State Mining Readiness Index in India has how many Indicators?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The State Mining Readiness Index (राज्य खनन तत्परता सूचकांक) in India is built on 4 broad indicators/pillars.

• It was released by the Ministry of Mines to assess and rank states on their mining sector performance and readiness.

• The index helps promote competitive federalism and ease of doing business in the mining sector.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The index evaluates states on parameters such as regulatory framework, ease of clearances, infrastructure and sustainability.

• It supports the goal of increasing the mineral sector's contribution to India's GDP.

NOTE

• 6 (Option 2): Incorrect number of indicators for the index.

• 7 (Option 3): Incorrect number of indicators for the index.

• 9 (Option 4): Incorrect number of indicators for the index.

question: The first-ever Export Preparedness Index in India was launched in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2020.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first-ever Export Preparedness Index (EPI) (निर्यात तैयारी सूचकांक) in India was launched in 2020.

• It was released by NITI Aayog in association with the Institute of Competitiveness.

• It ranks Indian states and Union Territories on their export potential and performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The EPI is based on four pillars: Policy, Business Ecosystem, Export Ecosystem and Export Performance.

• Gujarat topped the first EPI 2020 rankings among states.

NOTE

• 2018 (Option 1): The EPI was not launched in this year.

• 2005 (Option 2): Incorrect launch year for the EPI.

• 2015 (Option 3): Incorrect launch year for the EPI.

question: Where are the headquarters of the National Anti Doping Agency of India situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) (राष्ट्रीय डोपिंग रोधी एजेंसी) of India has its headquarters in New Delhi.

• It was established in 2005 to promote dope-free sports in India.

• It functions under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• NADA operates in line with the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) code.

• The National Dope Testing Laboratory (NDTL), also in New Delhi, conducts sample analysis.

NOTE

• Bengaluru (Option 1): Not the location of NADA's headquarters.

• Kolkata (Option 2): Not the location of NADA's headquarters.

• Mumbai (Option 3): Marked wrong in the response sheet; NADA is headquartered in New Delhi, not Mumbai.

question: The two bird sanctuaries Sakkarakottai and Therthangal are in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sakkarakottai and Therthangal bird sanctuaries are located in Tamil Nadu (तमिलनाडु), in the Ramanathapuram district.

• They are important habitats for migratory and resident water birds.

• Tamil Nadu has one of the largest networks of bird sanctuaries in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous bird sanctuaries in Tamil Nadu include Vedanthangal (India's oldest) and Vettangudi.

• Tamil Nadu's capital is Chennai; it has a long coastline along the Bay of Bengal.

NOTE

• Gujarat (Option 1): Home to sanctuaries like Nal Sarovar, but not these two.

• Goa (Option 2): Has the Salim Ali Bird Sanctuary, not Sakkarakottai or Therthangal.

• Karnataka (Option 4): Has Ranganathittu Bird Sanctuary, not these two.

question: The first senior National Handball Championship was held at Rohtak (Haryana) in _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1972.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first senior National Handball Championship in India was held at Rohtak, Haryana in 1972 (1972 में रोहतक).

• Handball is a fast team sport played by two teams of seven players each.

• The Handball Federation of India governs the sport in the country.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Handball became an Olympic sport (indoor format) at the 1972 Munich Olympics.

• A standard handball match consists of two halves of 30 minutes each.

NOTE

• 1992 (Option 1): Not the year of the first National Handball Championship.

• 1932 (Option 2): Incorrect year for the first championship.

• 1942 (Option 3): Incorrect year for the first championship.

question: From the following authors, who created 'Midnight's Children'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salman Rushdie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Midnight's Children was written by Salman Rushdie (सलमान रुश्दी) and published in 1981.

• It won the Booker Prize (1981) and later the 'Booker of Bookers'.

• The novel links the birth of its protagonist Saleem Sinai to India's independence at midnight on 15 August 1947.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Salman Rushdie's other notable works include 'The Satanic Verses' and 'Shame'.

• The novel is a landmark of magic realism in Indian English literature.

NOTE

• Raj Kamal Jha (Option 1): Author and journalist known for 'The Blue Bedspread'.

• Kiran Nagarkar (Option 3): Writer known for 'Cuckold' and 'Ravan and Eddie'.

• Upamanyu Chatterjee (Option 4): Author known for 'English, August'.

question:
Which of the following pair regarding monument – location is correct?
I. Golconda Fort – Rajasthan
II. Bharatpur Fort – Telangana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both given pairs are incorrectly matched, so the answer is Neither I nor II (न तो I और न ही II).

• Golconda Fort is located in Telangana (Hyderabad), not Rajasthan.

• Bharatpur Fort (Lohagarh Fort) is located in Rajasthan, not Telangana — the locations are effectively swapped.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Golconda Fort was the capital of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and is famous for its acoustics and diamond trade.

• Lohagarh Fort at Bharatpur, built by the Jats, was known for being virtually impregnable.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Wrong, as Golconda Fort is in Telangana, not Rajasthan.

• Only II (Option 2): Wrong, as Bharatpur Fort is in Rajasthan, not Telangana.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, since neither pairing is correctly matched.

question: In the context of Indian satellite launch vehicle, how many stages did GSLV-D1 has?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The GSLV-D1 (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) is a three-stage (तीन चरण) launch vehicle.

• Its first stage uses solid propellant, the second uses liquid propellant, and the third (cryogenic) stage uses liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen.

• GSLV-D1 was the first developmental flight of the GSLV, launched by ISRO in 2001.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The GSLV is used to place satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO).

• The PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) is a four-stage vehicle used for polar/sun-synchronous orbits.

NOTE

• Two (Option 1): Marked wrong in the response sheet; GSLV-D1 has three stages, not two.

• Five (Option 3): Incorrect number of stages for GSLV-D1.

• Six (Option 4): Incorrect number of stages for GSLV-D1.

question: What is inertia?
option_1: The ability of an object to change its velocity
option_2: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion
option_3: The force applied by an engine to move a vehicle
option_4: The force that pulls an object towards the Earth
solution_text:
The correct answer is The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Inertia (जड़त्व) is the tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion.

• It is described by Newton's First Law of Motion, also called the law of inertia.

• The inertia of a body is directly proportional to its mass — a heavier body has greater inertia.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Types of inertia: inertia of rest, inertia of motion, and inertia of direction.

• Newton's First Law: a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force.

NOTE

• The ability of an object to change its velocity (Option 1): This describes acceleration due to a force, not inertia.

• The force applied by an engine to move a vehicle (Option 3): Marked wrong in the response sheet; this is a thrust/force, not inertia.

• The force that pulls an object towards the Earth (Option 4): This describes gravity, not inertia.

question: In early 2025, the planets in a 'planetary parade' appeared lined up in the order of their _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is distance from the Sun.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a planetary parade (ग्रह परेड), planets appear lined up in the sky in the order of their distance from the Sun.

• Early 2025 saw several planets visible together in the night sky along the ecliptic.

• A planetary alignment is a visual/line-of-sight phenomenon, not a perfect physical straight line.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The order of planets from the Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

• Such alignments occur because the planets orbit the Sun roughly in the same plane (the ecliptic).

NOTE

• size (Option 1): Marked wrong in the response sheet; the parade order reflects distance, not size.

• brightness (Option 2): Brightness varies and is not the basis of the parade's line-up order.

• orbital speed (Option 3): Orbital speed is not the criterion for the parade arrangement.

question: Nagaur was conquered and annexed by which house of Rajputs during late Mughal period?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jodhpur.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nagaur was conquered and annexed by the Rathore house of Jodhpur (जोधपुर) (Marwar) during the late Mughal period.

• Jodhpur (Marwar) was ruled by the Rathore Rajput clan.

• Nagaur lies in the Marwar region of present-day Rajasthan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Jodhpur was founded by Rao Jodha in 1459 and is famous for the Mehrangarh Fort.

• Marwar's rulers, including Maharaja Jaswant Singh and Ajit Singh, were prominent in Mughal politics.

NOTE

• Mewar (Option 1): The Sisodia Rajput kingdom centred at Chittor/Udaipur, distinct from Nagaur.

• Amber (Option 2): The Kachhwaha Rajput state near Jaipur, not the annexer of Nagaur.

• Bikaner (Option 3): Another Rathore state, but Nagaur was annexed by Jodhpur, not Bikaner.

question: In India, who was the initial head of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board?
option_1: Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister
solution_text:
The correct answer is Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) (विदेशी निवेश संवर्धन बोर्ड) was initially headed by the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister.

• It was set up in the early 1990s under the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) to facilitate FDI.

• It later functioned under the Ministry of Finance (Department of Economic Affairs).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The FIPB approved FDI proposals requiring government approval on a case-by-case basis.

• The FIPB was abolished in 2017 as most sectors were opened to the automatic FDI route.

NOTE

• Finance Minister (Option 2): Marked wrong in the response sheet; the FIPB was later under the Finance Ministry but was initially headed by the Principal Secretary to the PM.

• External Affairs Minister (Option 3): Did not head the FIPB.

• Home Minister (Option 4): Did not head the FIPB.

question: The Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (BCSBI) was set up on 18th February _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2006.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Banking Codes and Standards Board of India (BCSBI) (भारतीय बैंकिंग संहिता एवं मानक बोर्ड) was set up on 18 February 2006.

• It was an independent autonomous body to monitor and ensure that banks follow codes and standards for fair customer service.

• It was set up on the recommendation of a committee headed by S.S. Tarapore.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• BCSBI was registered as a society and functioned with support from the RBI.

• It was wound up in 2021, with its codes integrated into the RBI's regulatory framework.

NOTE

• 2000 (Option 1): Incorrect year of BCSBI's establishment.

• 2002 (Option 2): Incorrect year of BCSBI's establishment.

• 2008 (Option 4): Incorrect year of BCSBI's establishment.

question:
Who among the following criticised the Moderates for their "politics of prayer"?
I. Bepin Chandra Pal
II. Bal Gangadhar Tilak
III. Lala Lajpat Rai
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II and III.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Extremists (Lal-Bal-Pal) — Bepin Chandra Pal, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Lala Lajpat Rai — all criticised the Moderates for their "politics of prayer" (निवेदन की राजनीति).

• They regarded the Moderates' methods of petitions, prayers and appeals to the British as ineffective.

• They advocated Swaraj, Swadeshi, boycott and national education.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The trio Lal-Bal-Pal led the assertive/extremist phase of the national movement (1905–1919).

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak famously declared, 'Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it.'

NOTE

• Only I and II (Option 1): Incomplete, as Lala Lajpat Rai also criticised the Moderates.

• Only II and III (Option 2): Incomplete, as Bepin Chandra Pal also criticised the Moderates.

• Only I and III (Option 3): Incomplete, as Bal Gangadhar Tilak also criticised the Moderates.

question: Which article of the Indian Constitution is related with the Duty of the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 355.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 355 (अनुच्छेद 355) imposes a duty on the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance.

• It also ensures that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

• It provides the constitutional basis for the imposition of President's Rule under Article 356.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Articles 355 and 356 fall under the emergency-related provisions concerning Centre-State relations.

• Article 356 deals with the imposition of President's Rule in case of failure of constitutional machinery in a State.

NOTE

• Article 348 (Option 1): Relates to the language to be used in the Supreme Court and High Courts.

• Article 352 (Option 2): Marked wrong in the response sheet; it deals with the proclamation of National Emergency.

• Article 361 (Option 4): Provides protection to the President and Governors regarding official acts.

question: During 1911-1921, what kind of population growth was recorded in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Negative population growth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During 1911–1921, India recorded negative population growth (ऋणात्मक जनसंख्या वृद्धि) — the only decade in modern census history to do so.

• The decline was caused by epidemics like the influenza (Spanish flu) pandemic of 1918, famines and poor health conditions.

• Hence 1921 is called the 'Year of the Great Divide' in India's demographic history.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• After 1921, India's population began rising steadily; 1921 marks the demographic transition.

• India's first census was conducted in 1872 and the first synchronous census in 1881.

NOTE

• High population growth (Option 1): Characterised later decades, not 1911–1921.

• Steady population growth (Option 3): Does not describe the decline of the 1911–1921 decade.

• Population explosion (Option 4): Refers to the rapid growth seen after independence, not 1911–1921.

question:
Which of the following tax (now replaced by GST) was levied by Central government?
I. Entertainment tax
II. Entry tax
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Entertainment tax and Entry tax were levied by State/local governments, not the Central government, so the answer is Neither I nor II (न तो I और न ही II).

• These state-level indirect taxes were subsumed into the Goods and Services Tax (GST) from 1 July 2017.

• GST replaced multiple central and state indirect taxes with a unified tax structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Central taxes subsumed under GST included central excise duty, service tax and additional customs duties (CVD/SAD).

• State taxes subsumed included VAT, entertainment tax, entry tax, luxury tax and purchase tax.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Wrong, as entertainment tax was a state tax, not a central tax.

• Only II (Option 2): Marked wrong in the response sheet; entry tax was levied by states/local bodies, not the Centre.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Wrong, since neither tax was levied by the Central government.

question: _____ was an ambassador who was sent to the court of Chandragupta by the Greek ruler of West Asia.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Megasthenes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Megasthenes (मेगस्थनीज) was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator (Greek ruler of West Asia) to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

• He wrote the book 'Indica', describing the society, administration and geography of Mauryan India.

• His account is a key foreign source for the Mauryan period.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire around 322 BCE with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya).

• 'Indica' survives only in fragments quoted by later Greek and Roman writers.

NOTE

• Al-Biruni (Option 1): A scholar from Central Asia who came with Mahmud of Ghazni and wrote 'Kitab-ul-Hind' (11th century).

• Ibn Battuta (Option 2): A Moroccan traveller who visited during Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq's reign (14th century).

• Marco Polo (Option 3): A Venetian traveller who visited South India in the late 13th century.
